notes: Independently inspected official editorial/author pages for all 16 candidates (10 discovery plus 6 expansion), read the fee audit, and used only difficulty, metrics and audit_note replacement fields. No fee routes were edited.

Bands are explicitly agent judgments about stated editorial contribution gates within relevant computing specialties. They are not measured individual acceptance probabilities, a cross-discipline prestige order, or guarantees. Unknown is deliberate where evidence does not calibrate relative selectivity.

Citation metrics, review-process targets, preparation burden and software maturity are separate from selectivity. EISEJ citation values are journal-reported with exact metric years; underlying provider denominators are unavailable on the inspected page. No impact factor was used to assign a difficulty band.

JAIR 10.6%/55.9% are the official model outputs for an initial-submission/revised-resubmission path, including a six-week resubmission assumption. The conditional population excludes summary rejections. The process-diagram image was blocked, so raw branch counts and complete calculations remain unverified; no raw acceptance rate or reconstructed count is supplied.

JMLR historical 17% wording and JOT 2010 approximately 30% were excluded from numeric metrics because observation windows/cohorts are underspecified. JOSS 2023 stage rejection estimates were excluded because denominators and periods are not precise and the 2026 criteria changed. Its linked current analytics timed out.

TheoretiCS official statistics are dated April 2026. The 2025 counts have 19 pending submissions and mix different cohorts if combined incorrectly; no acceptance ratio was calculated. The phase-1 strongest-contribution gate, not these incomplete counts, supports its band.

This was a bounded official-source search, not proof that no other metrics exist. Empty metric arrays mean no sufficiently defined numerical metrics were established here. Agent review is not human scientific review.
